questions.code:
CREATE TABLE tasks (id integer, name varchar(10), priority varchar(10));
INSERT INTO tasks VALUES (1,'alpha','low'),(2,'bravo','high'),(3,'charlie','mid'),(4,'delta','high');

SELECT name
FROM tasks
ORDER BY CASE priority
           WHEN 'high' THEN 1
           WHEN 'mid'  THEN 2
           ELSE 3
         END,
         name DESC
FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY;

-- tasks
-- id | name    | priority
--  1 | alpha   | low
--  2 | bravo   | high
--  3 | charlie | mid
--  4 | delta   | high

query.explanation: The CASE expression maps 'high' to 1, 'mid' to 2 and everything else to 3, so the two 'high' rows (bravo, delta) come first. The tie is broken by name DESC, which puts delta ahead of bravo, and FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY keeps just that row.
